item.text: {"text":"Temporal attention has relevant precedents, but these do not establish gains on the pinned Amazon benchmark. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) models positions and clipped, user-normalized pairwise time intervals; its temporal mechanism is relevant without adopting its causal backbone. [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute/relative temporal and positional embeddings with temporal-proximity contrastive learning. [ScaleRec (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596) addresses preferences at multiple scales, using a learnable Gaussian locality kernel and adaptive aggregation. These support testing temporal weighting while retaining older interactions, rather than assuming recency alone captures intent.\n\nA directly related [2026 BERT4Rec study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-026-01554-z) jointly trains a long-sequence encoder, time-aware session branch, and gate; continuous decay and content relevance balance immediate and durable interests. For this experiment, a simpler inference from the literature is to add per-head learned relative-position and bucketed elapsed-time biases inside the existing bidirectional BERT4Rec. Use only observed history timestamps; give the appended mask a learned unknown-time relation, never the unavailable target timestamp. Preserve masked-target training, final-nonpadding readout, and one jointly trained checkpoint per category. Compare position-only and position-plus-time variants separately against the corrected baseline using fixed macro validation HR@10 before combining interventions. Whether learned temporal weighting outperforms context deletion remains an empirical question."}
